content: Menyanthes is a genus of flowering plants that contains only one species, classified under the family Menyanthaceae. The name Menyanthes is derived from the Greek words menyein, meaning disclosing, and anthos, meaning flower. This name refers to the sequential manner in which the flowers on the plant's inflorescence open. The species Menyanthes trifoliata is distinguished by its horizontal rhizome and its alternate, trifoliate leaves. The plant produces an erect raceme of white flowers as its inflorescence. Menyanthes trifoliata is typically found in wetland habitats such as bogs and marshes across Asia, Europe, and North America. In North America, a specific form of this plant is often referred to as Menyanthes trifoliata var. minor Michx. This plant is commonly known in English as bog-bean or buckbean. In German, it is referred to as Bitterklee or Fieberklee.
